note: Faithful rendering of a difficult apoha passage, verses correctly set as verse; the inline pradhāna gloss is unmarked but correct.

errors.english: even if at a later time it is conditioned by the empowering influence of the object or the sense faculty
errors.why: The object or the sense faculty is what is altered by an empowering influence (absolutive + instrumental); the influence is not the object's or the faculty's.

fix.find: even if at a later time it is conditioned by the empowering influence of the object or the sense faculty
fix.replace: even if at a later time the object or the sense faculty is conditioned by an empowering influence

errors.english: will be explained once the defining mark is absent
errors.why: The other kind (of absence) that has a ground, i.e. from the absence of dewlap etc., the marks of a cow, 'will be explained' (in chapter three); 'absent' belongs to the example, not to when it will be explained.

note: Sound and terminologically careful; one case-role slip at the opening and an awkward segmentation of the dewlap lemma.

errors.english: existence itself does not appear because it is isolated and separated from other things
errors.why: Existence does not appear devoid of isolation from the other, i.e. it appears only as isolated from it, which is why the absence of the other is known (as the next sentence says).

fix.find: existence itself does not appear because it is isolated and separated from other things
fix.replace: existence itself does not appear without being isolated from other things

errors.english: Is it not incorrect for the Mimamsaka
errors.why: Nothing in the Tibetan names a Mīmāṃsaka (dpyod pa pa); the subject skyes mo(s) is an obscure or corrupt reading and the school attribution is the translator's guess.

errors.english: is intended to produce its own aspect
errors.why: mngon par sems pa here is abhimāna, 'is (falsely) conceived as the producer of its own aspect', not 'intends to produce'; likewise the object is 'nothing but this conception', not 'what is intended'.

note: Follows the commentary's lemma structure but misreads key epistemological wording in the absence-cognition passage.

errors.english: Even while [note: my mind] was wavering, I did not let go of [note: my resolve].
errors.why: The subject continued from the previous side is 'that which harms me' (anger): though it stirred, I did not let it loose; it is not my mind wavering or my resolve being kept.

fix.find: Even while [note: my mind] was wavering, I did not let go of [note: my resolve].
fix.replace: Even while it [note: the anger that harms me] was stirring, I did not let it loose.

errors.english: Who is that wrongdoer who, though you were wavering, you did not let go?
errors.why: It is the harmer that was stirring while the Bodhisattva did not let it loose, not the Bodhisattva who wavered.

fix.find: Who is that wrongdoer who, though you were wavering, you did not let go?
fix.replace: Who is that harmer of yours which, though it was stirring, you did not let loose?

errors.english: [note: One remains unharmed], like the fading light of the moon at dawn.
errors.why: The verse says ill repute comes to such a person like the moon's light fading at dawn (contrasting with the next verse's fame growing like the waxing moon); the inserted 'remains unharmed' inverts the image.

note: Verse well segmented, but the referent of the key exchange (the anger that stirred and was held in) is lost and one verse's image is inverted.

errors.english: If he entrusts the work while perceiving her as a non-relative but has doubts
errors.why: The duṣkṛta case is a non-relative whom he perceives as NOT a non-relative (i.e. as a relative), or about whom he is in doubt; perceiving her as a non-relative is the naiḥsargika case just stated.

fix.find: If he entrusts the work while perceiving her as a non-relative but has doubts
fix.replace: If he entrusts the work to a non-relative while perceiving her as a relative, or while in doubt

errors.english: You were commanded by Udayin to process the wool.
errors.why: Gautamī answers that Udāyin gave (her) wool to process; there is no 'you'.

fix.find: You were commanded by Udayin to process the wool.
fix.replace: Udayin gave me wool to process.

errors.english: How did your hands become so wounded?
errors.why: bka' rmas pa is the honorific 'asked'; the question is simply 'How did this come about?', with no mention of wounds.

note: Vinaya vocabulary mostly right, but the dialogue speaker is garbled and the perception condition that defines the lesser offence is inverted.

errors.english: At that time, you will remember me, who am free from worldly existence.
errors.why: The ascetic's son asks to be remembered then for (his) freedom from existence; he is not already free, as the frame (he later attains arhatship from the Buddha) shows.

note: Good verse and prose rendering across the end of one jātaka and the start of the next; one doubtful verse line.

errors.english: this is how the convention is intended to be applied
errors.why: brda byed pa is the convention-maker (the mantra-maker, as the previous side glosses), and the result is fixed 'because he so intended'; the agent is lost.
The continuum transformed is that of the mantra (successive distinctions produced in what has been produced), not the practitioner's stream of consciousness; the note misleads.

note: Clear and accurate on the mantra-efficacy argument apart from the agent of the convention and a misleading note on rgyud.

errors.english: Although the third characteristic of the reason is indeed established as known
errors.why: With tshul from the previous side this is tshul gsum pa'i rtags, the trairūpya mark (reason with three characteristics), not the third characteristic.

fix.find: Although the third characteristic of the reason is indeed established as known
fix.replace: Although the reason possessing the three characteristics is indeed established as known

errors.english: everywhere the probandum exists, the presence of the reason pervades it
errors.why: Anvaya is the presence of the probandum pervading the presence of the reason in all cases; the English swaps pervader and pervaded.

fix.find: everywhere the probandum exists, the presence of the reason pervades it
fix.replace: in all cases the presence of the probandum pervades the presence of the reason

note: Argument followed in outline, but two errors in core trairūpya/vyāpti terminology need a specialist's correction.

errors.english: If you say it is because that object is grasped
errors.why: Following the proximity objection, yul de(r) bzung ba means 'grasped in that same location', not 'that object is grasped'.

note: Sound rendering of the citra argument with verses and objections correctly marked.

errors.english: the very engagement of the cognition of an entity, by producing a discordant cause characterized as a latent impression, is cut off
errors.why: It is the cognition of absence that, by producing a discordant cause (a latent impression), cuts off the continuum of the entity-cognition; the English attaches 'producing' to the entity-cognition.

note: Careful and largely accurate on a dense passage about mutually exclusive conceptions.
